brief.headline: Lock a 10–15% price cut on caps by showing five credible alternates and pushing to market-fair levels; then ask for 15-day faster payment to free up ₹1.82 L cash.

priceAsk.summary: Ask for a 10–15% cut on our rigid plastic packaging (especially closures and caps), targeting the market-fair band.
priceAsk.target: Push our cap prices toward the ₹0.65–0.80/pc lower end of the market-fair band (market asks sit at ₹0.55–1.20/pc typical ₹0.85–0.95/pc).
priceAsk.basis: The open-market verdict is 'MARKET-FAIR; modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume / looser spec' — our volume and the five strong alternates we've lined up justify landing in that lower zone.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move terms from 30 days after receipt to 15 days after receipt.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Frees up ₹1.82 L cash for us.

brief.financialLeverage: Rachana Plastics publishes no financials, so we can't see their revenue, profit or how tight their cash is. That means we build our plan on what we do know: we spend ₹44.37 L a year with them, the market for this packaging is competitive, and we now have five credible alternates — three listed firms and two capable privates, including Manjushree Technopack (₹2569.83 Cr revenue, India's largest rigid-plastic converter). Without visibility into their books, we lean on competition and our readiness to qualify a second source. Push firmly on price and payment terms, but stay professional — we want the saving, not a fight with a supplier whose stability we can't measure.

evidence.point: We spend ₹44.37 L a year with Rachana — meaningful volume to command better terms.
Open-market ask for a 28 mm PP cap ranges ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typically ₹0.85–0.95/pc, with headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume.
The market verdict is 'MARKET-FAIR' — we're paying a fair rate today, but there's room to negotiate down.
evidence.figure: MARKET-FAIR; modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume / looser spec

evidence.point: HDPE resin import price is 87.61 ₹/kg — input-cost visibility supports our ask.
We currently pay 30 days after receipt; moving to 15 days faster frees ₹1.82 L for us.
Manjushree Technopack, India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter, is a proven alternate (₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health score 65/100).

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter (₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health 65/100) — pharma bottles, caps, preforms; top second-source candidate already in our data.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader for pails, containers and pharma packaging — strong, profitable, a robust alternate for bottles and closures.

alternates.name: IVL Dhunseri Petrochem Industries Private Limited
alternates.why: A lead to qualify (verify before RFQ): manufacturer in India-East, medium confidence; potential upstream source for resin or preforms.

risks: Rachana publishes no financials — we can't see if they're healthy or cash-strapped, so watch for sudden quality slips or delivery delays that signal trouble.
Pushing too hard without knowing their financial state could fracture the relationship; keep tone firm but fair, and have the second source (Manjushree or Mold-Tek) ready to quote before the meeting.
The market-backup leads (IVL Dhunseri, Dalmia, Ganesha, Chemco, Srichakra, Reliance) are research finds, not qualified suppliers — verify capability and MOQ before issuing any RFQ.
If Rachana won't move on price or terms, be ready to split the ₹44.37 L spend: give half to a listed alternate (Mold-Tek or Pearl Polymers) to build leverage for the next round.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We've reviewed our packaging spend and the market — we'd like to work together on a 10–15% price improvement and faster payment terms, but we're also talking to Manjushree and Mold-Tek to ensure we have two strong sources in place.
